assessment_membership.source: C3-c authoring declaration (2026-09-27): this target is placed in the V1 placement bank's clarification-request set by this cut's authoring review. The declaration is made here — no authoring fixture and no external assessment export in this repository places this target, so the membership is this review's own and is recorded as such.

texts.text: A clarification request: the question a listener asks to have the other person explain the words or meaning that were not understood, addressed to the interlocutor rather than answered alone.

The question stands right after the words that were not understood: What do you mean by that? It is built with do-support (what do you mean, not what you mean) and can name the puzzling word with by (what do you mean by restructuring?) or echo the claim with a comma (what do you mean, the contract is void?). The question's whole point is the other person's answer: it hands the floor back for an explanation rather than guessing at the meaning.

Do-support is the drill: the question needs do (what do you mean), and learners drop it because their own language builds wh-questions without an auxiliary. The second slip is the trailing object — what do you mean that? bolts a demonstrative onto mean, which takes no such object; the echo use needs a comma (what do you mean, the contract is void?) and the by-phrase needs its noun (what do you mean by that?).

What do you mean asks for the other person's meaning; what do you mean to do asks about their intention and is a different question; do you mean ...? asks for a yes-or-no confirmation of a guessed meaning rather than an explanation. Why do you mean that? is not current English. Sorry, what does that mean? is the sibling request pointed at a word or phrase instead of the speaker's intended sense.
你是什么意思？（请对方解释自己没听懂的言下之意，把话轮交回给对方）

pedagogical_profile.rationale: Bands are the C3-c authoring judgement (V1 carries no calibration data): the question is the standard clarification move of the language, so receptive value and naturalness are HIGH and core utility is HIGH; productive value is HIGH because asking instead of guessing is a repair move every conversation needs. Productive difficulty is LOW: five fixed words. Transfer value is HIGH: the do-support question pattern transfers across the wh-family. RESOURCE_PRACTICE follows the entity's own declared learning_intent ESTABLISH. Revisit when Calibration100 response data exists.

pack_overlays.rationale: The question belongs to the general fluency pack (the phrases that repair a conversation), so it carries full weight in that pack's coverage accounting.

Asking a colleague or a client to explain a term or an instruction (what do you mean by restructuring?) is core workplace language, so the unit carries most of the workplace pack's weight; the reduced weight records that the pack's own review has not placed it.

example_policy.policy: Present at most two examples per attempt, whole sentences only: the canonical question first; a SUPPORTING or CONTRAST sentence only after the learner has attempted the canonical form twice without producing it. Always show the question with its do and with its by-phrase or comma-echo complete, never present the auxiliary-dropped or object-bolted form as a model of the question, and never present an ERROR_INSTANCE as a model.

typical_errors.error_pattern: what you mean? (the do-support auxiliary dropped from the question)
typical_errors.explanation: English builds wh-questions with do-support, and learners drop the auxiliary because their own language questions in place without one; what you mean is a statement word order with a question mark attached.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when the string what you mean stands as a question with no do and no subject-auxiliary inversion, followed by a question mark or a by-phrase.

typical_errors.error_pattern: what do you mean that? (a demonstrative bolted onto mean where no object belongs)
typical_errors.corrected_pattern: what do you mean? / what do you mean by that?
typical_errors.explanation: Mean in this question takes no direct object — the thing asked about arrives in a by-phrase or an echo — and learners bolt the demonstrative on because their own language objects the question word; the result is not a stored English pattern.
typical_errors.detection_policy: Match when the question carries mean that or mean this with no comma and no by, in a sentence where the question mark closes the string.

detection_policy.policy: Fires only on the learner's own produced English text, and only on a visible surface form: the auxiliary slot of the question and what follows mean. No model judgement and no confidence score participates (PRODUCT_CONTRACT §8.1: V1 does not treat a model's self-reported high confidence as an R4 certification). Each rule below states the positive direction it must match; the fixture with the same ordinal states a case the rule must NOT match, so every rule ships with a testable boundary. expected values are NO_MATCH (the shape is absent) and NO_MATCH_BOUNDARY (mean to is the intention reading, so the clarification request is not in use).

detection_rules.rule: AUXILIARY_DROP: match when the question runs what you mean with no do and no inversion, because English builds this question with do-support.
OBJECT_SLIP: match when the question carries mean that or mean this with no comma and no by, because mean takes its object in a by-phrase or an echo.

ACCEPTED_REALIZATIONS: do not match when the question stands whole (what do you mean by that?; what do you mean, the contract is void?), including with a sorry in front: those are the accepted realizations.

THE_INTENTION_READING: do not match when the question runs mean to + an infinitive (what do you mean to do about it?), because there the words ask about intention and the clarification request is not in use.

detection_fixtures.text: What do you mean by that?
What do you mean, the contract is void?
Sorry, what do you mean by restructuring the whole team?
What do you mean to do about the cancelled order?
What you mean by that? The deadline is still Monday, no?
What do you mean that? I thought the contract was signed.
